assumptions.slippage_model: Taker: walk each venue's order book for the notional; slippage = average fill vs book mid, on entry and exit. Maker: slippage assumed zero and fills are not guaranteed. A book too thin for the notional is marked insufficient liquidity and excluded from rankings.
assumptions.funding_model: Current hourly-normalized funding rate is assumed to persist for the whole period. Positive rate: longs pay shorts. Funding, basis and liquidity change; these are estimates.
notes: Estimates, not profit or guaranteed arbitrage. Information only.
Past funding does not predict future funding.
Stale venue data (older than 5 minutes) is excluded from rankings.

disclaimer: Estimates only, not financial advice. Funding, prices and liquidity change; results are not guaranteed.
headline: Last 30 days: Strike XRP, SOL, PUMP and ETH longs were cheaper to hold than on other venues in most hours, but shorts cost more.

key_findings.title: Strike perps below index: longs cheaper, shorts costlier
key_findings.text: Strike's XRP, SOL, PUMP and ETH perps traded below their index price in most hours (Sep 21 to Oct 21; Strike funding was negative in 80%, 80%, 59% and 63% of hours). Longs were cheaper to hold on Strike than on the other venues in most hours, and shorts were more expensive.
details: XRP: Strike funding negative in 80% and positive in 20% of hours; Strike cheaper for longs in at least 97% and for shorts in at least 3% of hours.
SOL: Strike funding negative in 80% and positive in 20% of hours; Strike cheaper for longs in at least 90% and for shorts in at least 7% of hours.
PUMP: Strike funding negative in 59% and positive in 41% of hours; Strike cheaper for longs in at least 77% and for shorts in at least 6% of hours.
ETH: Strike funding negative in 63% and positive in 37% of hours; Strike cheaper for longs in at least 72% and for shorts in at least 15% of hours.
key_findings.caveat: A discount or premium to index can change quickly, and it also affects entry and exit prices (basis). Past funding does not predict future funding.

summary: Over the last 30 days, Strike was the cheaper venue for 48% of hours for BTC shorts vs Hyperliquid, 51% vs OKX (funding only).
Over the last 30 days, Strike was the cheaper venue for 52% of hours for BTC longs vs Hyperliquid, 49% vs OKX (funding only).
Over the last 30 days, Strike was the cheaper venue for 15% of hours for ETH shorts vs Hyperliquid, 28% vs OKX (funding only).
slippage_note: Slippage per fill is the current order-book walk at the report notional (average of buy and sell, floor 2 bps). It reflects current depth, not historical depth.

report_assumptions.slippage_note: Slippage per fill is the current order-book walk at the report notional (average of buy and sell, floor 2 bps). It reflects current depth, not historical depth.
report_assumptions.low_confidence_rule: Low confidence: thin liquidity or extreme funding: |30-day net| above 5% of notional, or book thin at the notional. Flagged pairs stay in the tables but are excluded from the summary.
notes: Past funding does not predict future funding.
Round-trip costs are paid once; cumulative net adds hourly carry on top.
Hours missing on either venue are skipped, never counted as zero funding.
OKX payments are spread evenly over the hours of their interval.
Basis and execution prices at close are not modelled.
